title: compact-feature-kits-playbook-scratch
content:
Purpose
---
Working sketch for a lightweight "Feature Kit" concept: composable, pre-configured LLM building blocks that product teams can assemble (no infra changes) to rapidly ship small, opinionated LLM experiences (summarize + highlight + Q&A, extract entities, short-form rewrite, etc.). Target is PMs/PDs/PMM and engineers who want fast prototyping with predictable latency and cost envelopes.

Problem we see
---
- Teams frequently build the same three mini-features (summaries, highlights, short Q&A, extraction) but each rollout requires bespoke prompts, model choices, batching, and safety configs.
- Non-engineering stakeholders lack simple knobs to trade off latency/cost/quality for each feature variant.
- Slow prototyping means duplicates of prompt engineering and infra work across products.

Hypothesis
---
If we provide a catalog of small, composable "feature kits" (each is: prompt template(s), validation tests, quality baseline, SLO presets, and recommended model/quantization), product teams will iterate 2–3x faster and we will reduce per-feature onset cost by ~30% (less time on infra tuning and prompt rewrites).

Goals
---
- Minimal: a UI + API to pick and wire 2–4 kits into a product flow and get a deployable spec.
- Provide 3 default SLO profiles per kit: fast (low-cost), balanced (default), high-quality (latency-cost higher).
- Each kit ships with a tiny eval suite (10 prompts, rough QA checklist) so teams can detect regressions.
- Offer exportable config (JSON) for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Non-goals (for MVP)
---
- Not building a full no-code app composer. MVP is a checklist + small catalog + API to return config.
- Not automating model fine-tuning. Kits only recommend models/quantized variants.

Target personas
---
- PM/Prototyper (non-dev): wants a quick assemble-and-test experience, cares about time-to-feedback and cost.
- Product Engineer: needs predictable latency and packaged config for infra handoff.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): customization for enterprise customers with Private/Dedicated.

Example kits (MVP set)
---
1) One-paragraph summarizer: input doc -> concise paragraph (config: max_tokens, temperature, stop tokens)
2) Highlight + explain: extract 3 salient sentences + short explanation
3) Chat-guided Q&A (document-context aware): short answers, source citation hints
4) Entity-extract-lite: return list of canonical entities with types (compact JSON)
5) Rewrite-tone: short text rewriting to a target persona/tone

Kit payload (what a kit contains)
---
- id, human-friendly name, description
- canonical prompt templates with variables and examples
- recommended model family + quantization profile
- SLO presets: fast/balanced/high-quality (token limits, max latency, batch strategy)
- tiny eval set (10 examples) + target metrics (F1-like for extraction, ROUGE-ish for summarization)
- safe-fallback behavior (if hallucination risk > threshold -> fall back to conservative template or smaller response)
- suggested telemetry keys (latency, cost_per_call, model_used, eval_score)

User stories (rough)
---
- As a PM, I want to assemble a Summarizer + Highlight kit into a product UI so I can demo a compact "digest" feature to stakeholders in <1 day.
- As an engineer, I want to export kit config so I can pin it to Dedicated capacity with the same SLOs as the hosted preview.
- As an SE, I want to run the kit's eval suite on the customer's private corpus and see a pass/fail suggestion.

API + UX sketch
---
- UX: simple catalog page, kit details, "Add to canvas" -> small flow builder that connects input source -> kit -> output. Tiny preview pane to run example inputs.
- API: POST /v1/feature-kits/preview {kit_id, profile: fast|balanced|hq, inputs: []} -> streaming output + metrics.
- Export: GET /v1/feature-kits/export/{config_id} -> JSON with prompt templates, model hints, SLOs for infra.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
---
- Catalog with at least 4 kits and sample preview UI.
- API preview endpoint that returns stable outputs for the 10 eval cases.
- Exported config validated by infra team for Dedicated compatibility.
- Basic telemetry emitted for preview runs: latency, token_count, model_hint.

Observability / Metrics
---
- Kit adoption: number of distinct projects using kits, preview -> export conversion rate.
- Per-kit eval score trendline, preview latency distribution, cost per preview.
- Failures: percent of previews hitting fallback because hallucination heuristics triggered.

Risks & mitigations
---
- People will treat kits as universal: add clear docs and example delimiters for "when not to use".
- Quality regressions from model swaps: require eval-suite pass threshold for auto-suggested model changes.
- UX complexity: keep canvas minimal; focus on 1-path flows rather than arbitrary DAGs.

Experiment ideas
---
- A/B test: kit-based prototype vs. ad-hoc prompt prototype (time to first demo, number of prompt edits).
- Measure cost delta when using "fast" profile vs. balanced in real usage for 3 customers.

Open questions
---
- What is the smallest set of eval metrics that meaningfully predict user satisfaction for each kit?
- Should kits include default moderation hooks or make that optional per kit?
- How will rate-limiting and burst policies interact with kit SLO presets? (need SRE input)

Next steps (short list)
---
- Sync with Solutions Eng + Infra: can we formalize an export schema for Dedicated by 2026-03-15? (Evan)
- Build 4 prototype kits and a barebones preview API (Mika owning). Target internal demo in 3 weeks.
- Draft kit authoring guide (how to write prompts, create evals, choose SLOs).

Notes to self (random)
---
- Consider a "kit marketplace" later where teams can publish vetted kits internally.
- Keep exports backward compatible: add version field early.
- Link to related ideas: mini-runway, prompt-tiles, micro-pipeline-playbook (internal overlap).
